fixture_note: Adversarial: an operator raises a run-level boundary flag. Expected outcome HALT at conflict-resolution precedence 1, overriding an otherwise well-evidenced option. A boundary flag outranks every score, matching the Leverage Engine G4 semantics so the two systems agree on what stops a run.

intake.problem_statement: We must decide how to satisfy an urgent customer request for a bulk export of stored payment records to an external analytics vendor.
constraints: customer has escalated to the executive sponsor

options.label: Export the payment records to the vendor
options.mechanism: Extract the stored payment records in bulk and transfer them to the vendor's ingestion endpoint under the existing data-processing agreement.
options.tradeoff: Moves regulated payment data outside the current processing boundary.

options.label: Send derived aggregates only
options.mechanism: Compute the metrics the vendor needs inside our own boundary and transfer only the non-identifying aggregate results.
options.tradeoff: The vendor cannot run analyses we have not anticipated, so later requests need new work.

evidence_register.locator: DPA section 4: processing is limited to derived metrics
evidence_register.claim_supported: The agreement does not cover bulk record transfer.

evidence_register.locator: the export set contains stored primary account numbers
evidence_register.claim_supported: The export set contains regulated payment identifiers.

evidence_register.locator: internal standard: regulated payment data does not leave the processing boundary
evidence_register.claim_supported: Bulk export is prohibited by internal standard.

primitives.statement: The export set contains stored primary account numbers.
The processing agreement covers derived metrics only.
The vendor's stated analysis needs are not fully enumerated.

claims.statement: The requested transfer would move regulated identifiers outside a boundary that the governing agreement does not extend to.
Derived aggregates satisfy the stated analytical need inside the existing agreement.

options.label: Export the payment records to the vendor
options.mechanism: Extract the stored payment records in bulk and transfer them to the vendor's ingestion endpoint under the existing data-processing agreement.
options.tradeoff: Moves regulated payment data outside the current processing boundary.

options.label: Send derived aggregates only
options.mechanism: Compute the metrics the vendor needs inside our own boundary and transfer only the non-identifying aggregate results.
options.tradeoff: The vendor cannot run analyses we have not anticipated, so later requests need new work.

options.label: Let the vendor query inside our boundary
options.mechanism: Grant the vendor a scoped query interface that runs against the records without any data leaving the processing environment.
options.tradeoff: Requires building and operating a query surface that does not exist today.

claims.statement: Three mechanisms exist: move the data, move a derivative of the data, or move the computation to the data.

defects.statement: The request treats an escalation as authority to widen the processing boundary, which no evidence in this run grants.
defects.remediation: Obtain an amended data-processing agreement before any bulk transfer is considered.

claims.statement: Executive escalation is not a source of processing authority, so the export option has no lawful basis in the evidence supplied.

effects.statement: Exporting once under escalation establishes escalation as a route around the processing boundary, so the boundary stops functioning as a control.
Delivering aggregates sets the expectation that analytical needs are met by derivation, which reduces the volume of future raw-data requests.
effects.follows_from: Aggregates are delivered instead of records.

claims.statement: Meeting the need by derivation reduces the volume of later raw-data requests rather than inviting them.

relations.mechanism: the pipeline delivers to the vendor endpoint
vendor processing is bounded by the agreement
the agreement determines what may leave the store

feedback_loops.effect: The agreement is the only balancing element in the loop, so a transfer that exceeds it leaves the loop with no control element at all and the data cannot be recalled.

claims.statement: The processing agreement is the sole balancing element in this loop, so a transfer exceeding it removes the only control rather than stressing it.

failure_modes.statement: The transferred records are retained or replicated inside the vendor environment and cannot be recalled.
failure_modes.precondition: The vendor's retention behaviour is not contractually bounded for record-level data.
failure_modes.detection_signal: Vendor storage growth proportional to the transferred record count.

failure_modes.statement: The aggregates are computed on a stale snapshot and the vendor draws conclusions from outdated figures.
failure_modes.precondition: The aggregation job is run once and never scheduled.

failure_modes.statement: The scoped query surface is built with insufficient row-level restriction and becomes an indirect export path.
failure_modes.precondition: Query results are not bounded to non-identifying aggregates.
failure_modes.detection_signal: Query result sizes approach the underlying record count.

claims.statement: The export option carries the only irreversible failure mode, because transferred records cannot be recalled once replicated outside the boundary.
